subtopics.title: The Three Questions and the Test They Set

questions.question: The three economic questions every system must answer are:
options: WHAT to produce, HOW to produce it, and FOR WHOM to produce
Who governs, who votes and who taxes

questions.question: The underlying variable that separates one economic system from another is:
options: Who owns and controls the MEANS OF PRODUCTION, because ownership determines who has the right to decide

questions.question: In a country with very high unemployment, the HOW question is particularly sharp because:
options: There is nothing left to produce
The choice between labour-intensive and capital-intensive methods decides how many people work

questions.question: Why must an economic system not be confused with a political system?
options: Because economic systems are chosen by voters
Because political systems have no effect on the economy
Because economic systems are classified by ownership and co-ordination, political systems by how power is held and transferred — two separate axes

questions.question: The price mechanism co-ordinates a free market because:
options: A rise in demand raises price, which raises profit, which attracts producers and resources, which expands supply — prices carrying both information and incentive
Producers agree on prices in advance
Consumers vote for prices each year

questions.question: In a free market, the FOR WHOM question is answered by:
options: INCOME — those with the most purchasing power obtain the most output
Length of service to the state

questions.question: Street lighting is under-supplied by a pure market because:
options: It is too expensive to produce
It is a PUBLIC GOOD — non-excludable, so nobody will pay for it voluntarily
It creates a positive externality for producers

questions.question: A factory polluting a river is a market failure because:
options: The factory earns too much profit
The factory does not pay for the damage it causes, so its price is wrong and too much is produced

questions.question: In a centrally planned economy, the WHAT question is answered by:
options: The central planning authority, according to its assessment of social need

questions.question: Which is a genuine strength of central planning, fairly stated?
options: National resources can be mobilised very rapidly toward a chosen objective, and basic needs can be guaranteed regardless of income
It responds instantly to changing tastes

questions.question: The INFORMATION problem in a planned economy means that:
options: No central office can know the millions of local facts about wants and costs that prices summarise automatically, so plans are always partly wrong

questions.question: Queues for some goods alongside warehouses of others occur under central planning because:
options: Administered prices cannot adjust, so shortages and surpluses are not corrected the way a market price would correct them

subtopics.title: The Mixed and Dualistic Economy — South Africa

questions.question: In a mixed economy, the FOR WHOM question is answered by:
options: Income earned in the market, then MODIFIED by redistribution through progressive tax, grants, free basic services and no-fee schools
Ability to pay alone, with no adjustment

questions.question: Which set of features shows South Africa to be a MIXED economy?
options: Only state ownership of all mines and factories

Constitutional protection of property alongside socio-economic rights, mostly private production alongside state-owned enterprises in electricity, rail and ports, market regulators, and large-scale redistribution
No government participation in the economy at all
Prices fixed by a central planning office

questions.question: A DUALISTIC economy is one in which:
options: A modern, formal, capital-intensive economy coexists with an informal, survivalist, low-productivity one inside the same country

questions.question: The structural causes of South Africa's dualism are best given as:
options: Differences in individual effort and ambition
The weather and the mineral endowment

Land dispossession and migrant labour, apartheid spatial planning that placed people far from economic centres, and an unequal education system that withheld the qualifications the formal economy demands

subtopics.title: Three Ways to Run the Kitchen

questions.question: The tuckshop, where vetkoek sell out and tomorrow more vetkoek appear, represents:
options: The free market — the till does the talking and your wallet decides your plate

questions.question: The feeding scheme, with one official setting the term's menu, represents:
options: The centrally planned economy — fairer plates, worse information

questions.question: A school running both a feeding scheme and a tuckshop is a model of:
options: The MIXED economy — which is what South Africa is

subtopics.title: What the Till Knows and the Memo Doesn't

questions.question: "A price is a message" means that:
options: Prices carry information about what people want and what is scarce, gathered automatically and for free from millions of transactions
Prices are set by government notice

questions.question: When a planner's guess is wrong, the mistake persists because:
options: The price cannot correct it — the price was fixed by the office rather than discovered in a market
There is no money in circulation

questions.question: The market's "one cruel habit" is that:
options: It only hears money — a hungry learner with no coins sends no message at all, which is why every country keeps a feeding scheme beside its tuckshop

questions.question: The office tower and the airtime table an hour away illustrate:
options: Dualism — a formal, capital-rich economy and a survivalist, informal one inside one country

questions.question: Why can the airtime seller not simply borrow and grow?
options: Because banks lend against collateral, and someone with nothing to pledge cannot borrow the very thing that would let her grow
Because she does not want to
Because interest rates are fixed by the state

questions.question: "Effort" is a poor explanation of dualism because:
options: The real separators are structural — concentrated ownership, distance from work, unequal schooling and the collateral barrier — none of which is about how hard anyone tries

questions.question: Grants, no-fee schools, free basic services, land reform, small-business finance and public transport are best described as:
options: Features of a purely planned economy
The deliberate mixed-economy attempts to build doors between the first and second economies
